summary: Wormhole is a side-predictor targeting branches inside nested loops whose outcomes correlate across iterations of the outer loop. By folding the linear branch history into a multidimensional matrix based on the inner loop's iteration count, it successfully exposes and predicts complex cross-iteration patterns like diagonals or identical behaviors with a low hardware cost.

state.name: WPT
state.entry_format: tag (tag_bits bits), conf (conf_bits bits), ranking (ranking_bits bits), length (length_bits bits), history (history_bits bits), counters (num_counters x counter_bits bits)
state.size_formula: wpt_entries * (tag_bits + conf_bits + ranking_bits + length_bits + history_bits + (num_counters * counter_bits))
state.indexing: Fully associative search by branch PC

state.name: InFlightQueue
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), wpt_idx (ceil(log2(wpt_entries)) bits), counter_idx (ceil(log2(num_counters)) bits), wormhole_pred (1 bit), instruction_age (8 bits)
state.indexing: FIFO, pushed at predict, popped at commit

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
branch_tag = branch_PC & ((1 << tag_bits) - 1)
match = -1
for i in range(wpt_entries):
    if WPT[i].tag == branch_tag:
        match = i
        break

if match != -1:
    entry = WPT[match]
    bit0 = (entry.history >> 0) & 1
    bit1 = (entry.history >> entry.length) & 1
    bit2 = (entry.history >> (entry.length - 1)) & 1
    bit3 = (entry.history >> (entry.length - 2)) & 1
    idx = (bit0 << 3) | (bit1 << 2) | (bit2 << 1) | bit3
    if use_32kb_indexing:
        bit4 = (entry.history >> 1) & 1
        bit5 = (entry.history >> (2 * entry.length)) & 1
        bit6 = (entry.history >> (2 * entry.length - 1)) & 1
        bit7 = (entry.history >> (2 * entry.length - 2)) & 1
        idx = (idx << 4) | (bit4 << 3) | (bit5 << 2) | (bit6 << 1) | bit7
    
    idx = idx % num_counters
    sat_value = entry.counters[idx]
    pred = (sat_value >= 0)
    
    if InFlightQueue.size < max_in_flight_branches:
        InFlightQueue.push(valid=True, wpt_idx=match, counter_idx=idx, wormhole_pred=pred, instruction_age=current_age)
    
    if entry.conf > 0 and abs(2 * sat_value + 1) >= prediction_threshold:
        return pred

if InFlightQueue.size < max_in_flight_branches:
    InFlightQueue.push(valid=False, wpt_idx=0, counter_idx=0, wormhole_pred=False, instruction_age=current_age)
return TAGE_prediction
algorithms.notes: The history bit selection depends on the configuration. The prediction requires the confidence to be > 0 and the saturating counter absolute value to exceed the threshold. sat_value is assumed to be a signed integer.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.notes: Confidence counter is only updated when the wormhole prediction differs from TAGE. History is updated at commit time, which assumes no speculative history recovery.

algorithms.name: allocate
algorithms.trigger: commit time, when statistical corrector identifies branch as problematic
algorithms.notes: Candidate branches must be inside a loop and frequently mispredicted by TAGE. Replaces the lowest ranked entry.

algorithms.name: recover
algorithms.notes: Unwinds the InFlightQueue. Entries for instructions that are squashed are discarded. Entries for instructions older than the squash point survive. WPT history is not unwound because it is only updated at commit.

host_interfaces.description: Program counter of the branch, used to index/search the WPT.
host_interfaces.fallback: Hash of the PC or truncated PC

host_interfaces.description: Total expected number of iterations for the current innermost loop, provided by the baseline loop predictor.
host_interfaces.fallback: 0 (implies not in a loop, disabling Wormhole allocation)

host_interfaces.description: Signal from the baseline statistical corrector indicating the branch is frequently mispredicted.
host_interfaces.fallback: Independent local confidence counter tracking mispredictions

host_interfaces.description: The direction prediction from the base TAGE predictor.
host_interfaces.fallback: Prediction from a simple bimodal predictor

host_interfaces.description: The resolved outcome of the branch.
host_interfaces.fallback: Resolved outcome at squash or retire

host_interfaces.description: Identifier or age of the branch instruction being predicted, pushed to the InFlightQueue.
Identifier or age of the oldest squashed instruction, used to flush younger entries from InFlightQueue.
host_interfaces.fallback: Flush entire InFlightQueue on any squash (pessimistic).

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: WPT: 7 entries * 1571 bits = 10997 bits. InFlightQueue: 192 entries * 21 bits = 4032 bits.
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: The paper states 10997 bits for the 32KB configuration. Our total is 15029 bits; we are over the paper's figure by 4032 bits because the paper omitted the in-flight metadata queue (InFlightQueue) required to pass the lookup index and prediction to the commit stage, which is necessary to avoid recomputing indexes with shifted history.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: TAGE components or the statistical corrector can shrink to pay for this at iso-storage.

unit_tests.name: walk_conf_counter
unit_tests.given: WPT has an entry 0 with conf=14. InFlightQueue has two entries for this branch with valid=True, wpt_idx=0, wormhole_pred=True. TAGE_prediction is False, branch_outcome is TAKEN. Call update 2 times.
unit_tests.expect: After the first update, WPT[0].conf is 15. After the second update, WPT[0].conf remains 15 (saturates).

unit_tests.name: walk_sat_counter
unit_tests.given: WPT has an entry 0 with counters[0]=14. InFlightQueue has two entries with valid=True, wpt_idx=0, counter_idx=0, wormhole_pred=True. branch_outcome is TAKEN. Call update 2 times.
unit_tests.expect: After the first update, WPT[0].counters[0] is 15. After the second update, WPT[0].counters[0] remains 15 (saturates without wrapping).

unit_tests.name: walk_ranking_counter
unit_tests.given: WPT has an entry 0 with ranking=6. LPT_TOTAL=10. Call allocate 2 times with the same branch_PC matching entry 0.
unit_tests.expect: After the first allocate, WPT[0].ranking is 7. After the second allocate, WPT[0].ranking remains 7.

unit_tests.name: predict_identical_behavior
unit_tests.given: use_32kb_indexing=False, WPT entry 0 matches branch_PC. length=10. history has bit0=1, bit10=1, bit9=1, bit8=1. counters[15]=10, conf=5. InFlightQueue is empty.
unit_tests.expect: predict computes idx=15, pushes an entry to InFlightQueue with valid=True, wpt_idx=0, counter_idx=15, wormhole_pred=True, and returns True.

unit_tests.name: recover_queue_flush
unit_tests.given: InFlightQueue has 3 entries with instruction_age 1, 2, and 3. squash_point is 1.
unit_tests.expect: recover removes entries with age 2 and 3, leaving only the entry with age 1.

open_questions: The signedness and initial values of the saturating counters are not explicitly stated; assumed signed 5-bit counters initialized to 0.
The initial value for the ranking counter when an entry is allocated is not explicitly specified; assumed to be 3.
The paper does not detail whether the history is updated speculatively at lookup time or non-speculatively at commit time. Assumed commit time update to avoid a complex history recovery mechanism.
